authorInfo.bio: Charles Michael Baggs (1806–1845) was a Roman Catholic bishop, controversialist, scholar and antiquary. He briefly served as the Vicar Apostolic of the Western District of England from 1844 to 1845.

description: "The Ceremonies of the Holy-Week at Rome" by Charles Michael Baggs is a detailed descriptive account of the rituals and practices observed during Holy Week in the Roman Catholic tradition, written in the mid-19th century. This work explores the various ceremonies held during this significant week, including those of Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, and Holy Saturday, detailing both their historical origins and their liturgical significance.
